findings.text: Pressing Continue never restarts the paused agent. `Cards.js:244-247` (the spend-gate branch) calls `agents.grant()` and returns without sending the agent any message. `Agent.grant()` (`Agents.js` ~1404) only raises the allowance and clears `gated`. The agent was interrupted, so it sits idle with more money and nothing tells it to go on. The brief says "grant() reopens the agent". After granting, send it one line (for example "Servex: the owner gave you $5 more; continue") with `revive: true`, the same way the generic path below does.

If the owner answers the card after the agent has left `live` (a Servex restart, or a stop), the answer is lost with an error. `Agents.grant()` (`Agents.js:503`) calls `this.get(id)`, which throws "No agent …", and `Cards.js:246` doesn't catch it, so `wake()` throws. Wrap it in a try, and revive the agent from the registry (as `send()` does) before granting.

The read-loop warning also goes to agents the gate doesn't cover. `tool_started()` (diff line 130-140) never checks `gated_role()`, so the front desk (assistants, the voice pair) gets "your spend is gated on results" after 40 reads. That message is wrong for them, and every unwanted message costs a paid turn, which is the opposite of what this task is for. Add `if (!this.gated_role()) return;` before the read counting.

The "step done" rule (diff line 73) counts any Bash command that mentions `task.jsonl` and `"done":`. So a read such as `grep '"done":' task.jsonl` counts as a result and unlocks $3. Tighten it to writes only (`>>`, `append_log`), or drop the Bash half of the rule.

The gate's state lives only in memory. The registry never writes `gate_row()`: nothing calls it, and `registry.js` has no `spend_gate`. So a revived or restarted agent starts over with a fresh $2, and the Sessions-grid column has no data to show. The task log already defers the column; carrying `gate_row()` into the registry row is the step it needs first.

A Claude agent is still checked only when a turn ends (`Agents.js` ~1486), so one long turn can spend well past $2 before the gate fires. The mastermind deferred pricing each call during the turn on purpose and logged that choice. Proof case 1 (`spend-gate-proof.mjs`) tests a Claude agent being interrupted mid-turn, which can't happen in real use until that deferred work lands.

Scope: this merge covers part of item 4 (card wiring, `budget_usd`, proofs), item 6 (`provider` added to the keys `reopen()` falls back on, `Agents.js:492`, which is correct and proven), and a regression proof for item 1. Items 2, 3, 5 and 7–13 are not in it, and neither is the accounting half of item 4 (`or-reconcile.mjs`, `or-cache-probe.mjs`). The task must not be closed as landed until they are done.

`spawn_agent` gains `budget_usd` only as a schema entry (`tools.js:244`); it reaches the agent only because `agents.spawn(args)` copies every argument onto it. It isn't in `reopen()`'s keys, so a row without a `spec` loses it on revive, the same kind of bug item 6 just fixed for `provider`.
